revision_rule.note: The 2012 class grammar lacks later alternatives and restrictions including final and dynamic-override specifiers and the revised constructor argument grammar.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no default superclass-argument expansion marker in class constructor argument lists.
The special default superclass-argument expansion construct in a constructor argument list does not exist in IEEE 1800-2017.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no constructor argument-list construct that expands superclass constructor arguments with default.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no default keyword mechanism that expands superclass constructor arguments into a subclass constructor argument list.
IEEE 1800-2012 lacks default superclass-constructor argument expansion, so its name-collision restriction is absent.
IEEE 1800-2017 lacks constructor default superclass-argument expansion, so it defines no associated argument-name collision rule.
IEEE 1800-2012 lacks default superclass-constructor argument expansion and its local-member default restriction.
IEEE 1800-2017 lacks constructor default superclass-argument expansion and its restriction on defaults referring to local members.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no default superclass-argument expansion keyword for subclass constructor argument lists.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not provide the default superclass-argument expansion keyword in constructor argument lists.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not state the later restriction limiting dependent :: type selection to typedefs, type operators, and type-parameter assignments.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not specify the restricted dependent class-scope type-selection rule for incomplete forward types, interface-based typedefs, and type parameters.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no dynamic override specifiers on class methods.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no dynamic override specifiers on class method declarations.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not support default as the sole extends-specifier argument or inherited implicit constructor signatures.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not permit default as the sole extends-specifier argument or define inherited implicit constructor arguments from it.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no default argument in an extends specifier and no corresponding user-constructor requirement.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no default extends-specifier argument and no corresponding requirement on a user-defined subclass constructor.
IEEE 1800-2012 requires the extern prototype and class-qualified out-of-block definition but has no initial, extends, or final method specifiers to preserve in the prototype.
IEEE 1800-2017 requires the extern prototype, qualifiers, full arguments, and class-scoped out-of-block definition, but has no initial, extends, or final override specifiers to preserve or omit.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no :final class specifier.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no :final class specifier or prohibition on extending a class marked by that construct.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no :final method specifier.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no :final method specifier or associated no-override rule.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no final specifier for methods or constraints.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no final method or constraint specifier, including on pure virtual declarations.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no constructor default argument expansion or implicit super.new(default) forwarding.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no constructor default argument expansion and therefore no implicit super.new(default) forwarding.
IEEE 1800-2012 makes dotted access to interface-class parameters illegal, rather than applying the ordinary class-handle parameter-access rules used in 2023.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no :extends method override specifier.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no :extends method override specifier.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no :initial method override specifier.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no :initial method override specifier.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no initial, extends, or final method override specifiers.
IEEE 1800-2017 has none of the :initial, :extends, and :final method override specifiers whose combinations this rule governs.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak-reference facility or strong, weak, and unreachable object classification.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak-reference facility or strong, weak, and unreachable object classification.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no default superclass-argument expansion marker and thus no directly-following constructor argument restriction.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no default expansion keyword in constructor argument lists and thus no rule for the argument immediately following it.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no super.new(default) constructor-argument forwarding construct.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no default constructor-argument expansion and does not permit super.new(default) forwarding.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no super.new(default) or constructor default-expansion requirement.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no super.new(default) construct or matching constructor-list expansion requirement.
IEEE 1800-2012 permits this in the listed class contexts but does not include the later standalone type(this) exception.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no strong/weak/unreachable object-state transitions or weak-reference-based reclamation rule.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no strong/weak reachability state model or weak-reference transition semantics.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak-reference object identification values for associative-array indexing.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak_reference class, object identification values, or weak ID indexing rule.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no built-in weak_reference class or API.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no built-in weak_reference class or its new, get, clear, and get_id API.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak references or atomic clearing guarantee.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak-reference facility or atomic automatic clearing guarantee.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak_reference class constructor.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak_reference class constructor.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak-reference get method for event controls.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak-reference get method usable in event controls.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak-reference get_id API.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak-reference get_id API.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak-reference object identification values or determinism rules.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines no weak-reference object IDs or deterministic ID semantics.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak-reference object ID uniqueness or reuse rule.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines no weak-reference object IDs or lifetime uniqueness guarantee.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak-reference get or clear semantics.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak-reference get or clear semantics.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak_reference wrapper class or wrapper garbage-collection semantics.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak_reference wrapper class or independent wrapper collection semantics.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak-reference constructor or null-construction warning rule.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak_reference constructor or null-referent warning behavior.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not declare a built-in weak_reference class in package std.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not declare a weak_reference class in package std.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no built-in parameterized weak_reference class or class-type parameter restriction.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no built-in parameterized weak_reference type.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no weak_reference wrapper objects or wrapper identity semantics.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no weak_reference wrapper objects or wrapper identity semantics.
